mainTopic: Whether קדשי מזבח can be made into חרמי כהנים: רב הונא's rule, its refutation, and עולא's reading of 'כל חרם'.
overview: The משנה teaches rules shared by קדשי מזבח (items set aside for the altar) and קדשי בדק הבית (items set aside for Temple upkeep). You cannot switch their holiness to another kind, but you may consecrate their value (הקדש עילוי) or declare them חרם. If they die, they are buried, though רבי שמעון says dead בדק הבית animals are redeemed. In the גמרא, רב הונא rules from a פסוק that attaching קדשי מזבח to חרמי כהנים does nothing. The גמרא first challenges him from a ברייתא that leaves out the altar case, and it defends him: the ברייתא lists only items that fail in both directions. A second challenge comes from the משנה's word 'מחרימין', and the גמרא answers that both words there mean בדק הבית. Two ברייתות then show plainly that קדשי מזבח can become חרמי כהנים, so רב הונא is refuted. עולא explains the פסוק differently: 'כל חרם' includes everything. The גמרא then questions whether עולא really holds this, since he elsewhere said that attaching an עולה to בדק הבית creates only an עיכוב. That discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Rules shared by altar-holy and Temple-upkeep-holy items
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists four rules that apply both to קדשי מזבח and to קדשי בדק הבית.
steps.simpleTranslation: MISHNA: Both items holy for the altar and items holy for Temple upkeep share these rules. You may not switch them from one kind of holiness to another. But you may consecrate their value, and you may declare them חרם. If they died, they must be buried.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה opens with rules that are the same for both types of holy items: altar items and Temple-upkeep items.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once something has one kind of holiness, you cannot move it into a different kind. However, you can still donate its 'value' (הקדש עילוי) or declare it חרם, so those words take effect in some way. Also, if a holy animal dies, it cannot simply be redeemed. It must be buried.

keyTerms.meaning: Things made holy for the altar, such as animals for קרבנות
Things made holy for the upkeep and repair of the בית המקדש
From one kind of holiness to another kind
Consecrating the value of an item to the Temple treasury
Declaring something חרם, meaning dedicated as a gift to the כהנים

phrases.english: MISHNA: Both items consecrated for the altar
and items consecrated for Temple maintenance:
one may not change them
from one sanctity to another sanctity,
but one may consecrate them with a consecration of value,
phrases.notes: The item stays as it was. What gets donated to the Temple treasury is its value.

phrases.english: and one may dedicate them as חרם,
and if they died, they must be buried.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶחָד קׇדְשֵׁי מִזְבֵּחַ וְאֶחָד קׇדְשֵׁי בֶּדֶק הַבַּיִת
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Neither type can be switched to another holiness. Both can receive הקדש עילוי and חרם. Both are buried if they die.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rule that you 'may declare them חרם' sets up the גמרא's discussion of רב הונא, who limits when a חרם on altar items works.

steps.title: רבי שמעון: dead Temple-upkeep animals can be redeemed
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון disagrees about the last rule. In his view, קדשי בדק הבית that died are redeemed, not buried.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון says: items holy for Temple upkeep, if they died, can be redeemed.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון argues on only the last rule of the משנה, the rule about animals that died.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion said that both kinds of holy animals must be buried when they die. רבי שמעון agrees about altar animals. But he holds that Temple-upkeep animals can be redeemed even after death.

keyTerms.meaning: They are redeemed, meaning exchanged for money that goes to the Temple
They must be buried

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says:
items consecrated for Temple maintenance,
if they died, they can be redeemed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disputes the final rule of the first opinion, about burying dead animals
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Dead קדשי בדק הבית animals are redeemed, not buried.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's shared rules: no switching holiness, הקדש עילוי and חרם both allowed, and burial if the animal dies. רבי שמעון makes an exception for בדק הבית animals that died.

steps.title: רב הונא: altar items attached to כהנים gifts do nothing
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא rules that if someone tries to attach קדשי מזבח to חרמי כהנים, nothing happens.
steps.simpleTranslation: GEMARA: רב הונא said: if someone took items holy for the altar and attached them to the gifts for the כהנים, he has done nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with רב הונא's ruling. Trying to turn altar-holy items into a חרם for the כהנים has no effect.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The person is trying to make something already holy for the altar into a gift for the כהנים. רב הונא says his words simply do not take effect.

keyTerms.meaning: He 'attached' them, meaning he used a vow to link the item to another holiness
Items declared חרם, which go to the כהנים
He has done nothing, meaning his words have no effect

steps.confusionAlert: The משנה just said 'מחרימין אותן', that you may declare holy items חרם, and רב הונא seems to say the opposite. Keep this tension in mind as the גמרא continues.

phrases.english: GEMARA: Rav Huna says:
items consecrated for the altar that one associated
with dedications for the priests,
he has done nothing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a ruling connected to the משנה's rule about חרם
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Attaching קדשי מזבח to חרמי כהנים has no effect.

steps.title: רב הונא's source from the פסוק about חרם
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for רב הונא's reason. It answers with a reading of the פסוק 'כל חרם קדש קדשים הוא לה׳'.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? The פסוק says: 'Every חרם is most holy to ה׳.' This means: any חרם made on something that is already 'most holy' must stay for ה׳.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רב הונא rules this way. It answers with a פסוק that he reads in a special way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא reads the words 'חרם קדש קדשים' as 'a חרם made on something that is already קדש קדשים'. The פסוק then says such a thing is 'לה׳', for ה׳. So it stays holy for the altar and does not go to the כהנים.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
Most holy, here read as items already holy for the altar

phrases.english: What is the reason?
The verse states:
'Every dedicated item is most holy to the Lord'
any dedication that is made on something most holy,
that should be for the Lord.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for רב הונא's ruling
steps.raayaObject: רב הונא's rule that a חרם on קדשי מזבח does not take effect
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא 27:28, read as 'a חרם on קדש קדשים remains for ה׳'

steps.title: Challenge begins: a ברייתא about Temple-upkeep items
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to challenge רב הונא. Its first case: קדשי בדק הבית attached to altar holiness or to חרמי כהנים does nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged him: items holy for Temple upkeep that someone attached, either to altar holiness or to the gifts for the כהנים, he has done nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: With 'מיתיבי' the גמרא starts quoting a ברייתא as a challenge to רב הונא. This line is still setting up the challenge. The clash itself comes in step 7.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא goes through each type of holiness one by one. In this first case, Temple-upkeep items cannot be moved into altar holiness or into a חרם for the כהנים.

keyTerms.meaning: Whether... or...

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
items consecrated for Temple maintenance that one associated,
whether with a consecration for the altar
or with a dedication to the priests,
he has done nothing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts quoting a ברייתא meant to challenge רב הונא
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's ruling that קדשי מזבח attached to חרמי כהנים does nothing
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא lists, one type at a time, what happens when each kind of holiness is attached to another. The case that contradicts רב הונא is drawn out in step 7.

steps.title: The ברייתא continues: כהנים gifts cannot be transferred
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא's second case: חרמי כהנים attached to altar holiness or to Temple-upkeep holiness does nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: Gifts for the כהנים that someone attached, either to altar holiness or to Temple-upkeep holiness, he has done nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא keeps going through its list. The גמרא is still building toward the case of קדשי מזבח, which is where the challenge to רב הונא will hit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here too, a חרם for the כהנים cannot be moved into any other holiness. Both cases so far end in 'he has done nothing'. This sets up the contrast with how the ברייתא will treat altar items.

keyTerms.meaning: Gifts for the כהנים that someone tried to attach to a different holiness

phrases.english: dedications to priests that one associated,
whether with a consecration for the altar
or with a consecration for Temple maintenance,
he has done nothing.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues quoting the same ברייתא with its next case
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא lists the 'does nothing' cases one by one. The case of altar items, where the contradiction with רב הונא lies, comes next.
steps.whatToRemember: So far the ברייתא says that בדק הבית items and חרמי כהנים cannot be transferred to other holiness. Watch for how it treats קדשי מזבח, since that is where it may clash with רב הונא.

steps.title: The ברייתא's silence seems to refute רב הונא
steps.stepSummary: Since the ברייתא only said that בדק הבית items and חרמי כהנים cannot be attached, it implies that קדשי מזבח attached to חרמי כהנים does take effect. That contradicts רב הונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: This implies that if someone attached altar-holy items to priestly dedications, what he did is done. That is a refutation of רב הונא!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its challenge from the ברייתא of steps 5–6. It reads the ברייתא's silence as proof that attaching קדשי מזבח to חרמי כהנים works, which goes against רב הונא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gave two cases that 'do nothing,' but it never mentioned קדשי מזבח. The גמרא infers that the missing case must take effect. רב הונא said it does nothing, so the גמרא calls this a תיובתא.

keyTerms.meaning: A strong refutation, a challenge that seems to knock down a view
He attached one item to another item's holiness, saying 'this should be like that'

phrases.english: This implies: altar-consecrated items
phrases.notes: The ברייתא listed only the two cases from steps 5 and 6, so the case it left out seems to work.

phrases.english: that one attached to priestly dedications
what he did is done (it takes effect),
a refutation of רב הונא!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion of the ברייתא challenge that steps 5–6 set up.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's ruling (step 3) that attaching קדשי מזבח to חרמי כהנים does nothing.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא lists only the cases that do nothing. Because קדשי מזבח is missing from the list, attaching it to חרמי כהנים must take effect.

steps.title: רב הונא explains why the altar case was left out
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא answers that the ברייתא left out קדשי מזבח because its ruling is split. Attaching it to בדק הבית works, but attaching it to חרמי כהנים does nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא would tell you: when the ברייתא left it out, it left it out for this reason. Altar items attached to Temple upkeep: what he did is done. But attached to priestly dedications, he did nothing.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא defends himself. The silence of the ברייתא does not prove that the altar case works in every direction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא's two items fail in both directions. קדשי מזבח does not fit that pattern, because it works with בדק הבית and fails with חרמי כהנים. So the ברייתא left it out on purpose, and רב הונא's ruling still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: He left it out (did not list it)
Holiness for the upkeep and repair of the בית המקדש
What he did takes effect
He did nothing; it has no effect

phrases.english: רב הונא could say to you:
when he (the תנא) left it out, he left it out because of this:
that altar-consecrated items which one attached to Temple upkeep —
what he did is done,
but if attached to priestly dedications —
he has done nothing.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains why the ברייתא left the case out: its ruling is split.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא's silence means altar items can be attached to anything, חרמי כהנים included.
steps.terutzMaskana: The altar case was left out because it works with בדק הבית but does nothing with חרמי כהנים.

steps.title: Then why not list the altar case with the others?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if attaching קדשי מזבח to חרמי כהנים does nothing, the ברייתא should have listed that half alongside its other 'does nothing' cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let him teach it together with those cases!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב הונא's answer. Even a split case could still have its 'does nothing' half listed in the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא is a list of attachments that fail. If קדשי מזבח to חרמי כהנים also fails, it seems to belong on that list. Leaving it out still looks strange.

keyTerms.meaning: So let him teach it
Together with those (other cases)

phrases.english: But let him teach it alongside those cases!
phrases.notes: 'Those cases' means the two cases from steps 5 and 6.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב הונא's answer in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 8 that the split ruling explains why the case was left out.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The 'does nothing' half could still have been listed with the other 'does nothing' cases.

steps.title: The תנא lists only items that fail both ways
steps.stepSummary: The תנא only lists items that cannot be attached in either of the two other directions. קדשי מזבח fails in only one direction, so it was not listed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The תנא teaches the cases that have two; the case that does not have two, he does not teach.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question of step 9. The list in the ברייתא follows a pattern, and the altar case does not fit it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בדק הבית items fail with both the altar and חרמי כהנים. חרמי כהנים fail with both the altar and בדק הבית. קדשי מזבח fails only with חרמי כהנים, so it does not fit the 'two' pattern, and רב הונא is safe from this ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: The teacher or author of the ברייתא
Two (here: two kinds of holiness it cannot be attached to)

steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא survives the ברייתא. The ברייתא lists only items that fail in both directions, and קדשי מזבח fails only with חרמי כהנים.

phrases.english: The תנא teaches the case that has two,
phrases.notes: 'Two' means two kinds of holiness that the item cannot be attached to.

phrases.english: the case that does not have two, he does not teach.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains how the list is built: it includes only items that fail in both directions.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Every 'does nothing' case should appear in the list.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only items blocked in both directions are listed. The altar case is blocked in one direction only.

steps.title: A challenge from our משנה: altar animals can be made חרם
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא cites the משנה: one may consecrate altar animals for their value (הקדש עילוי) and may make them חרם. The 'מחרימין' seems to mean חרמי כהנים, against רב הונא.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: 'One may consecrate them with a consecration of value.' Isn't 'consecration of value' for Temple upkeep, and 'one may dedicate them' for priestly dedications?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new challenge to רב הונא, this time from a משנה instead of a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lets a person apply two new holinesses to altar animals. The first, הקדש עילוי, matches בדק הבית. The second, מחרימין, seems to match חרמי כהנים, which would mean attaching altar items to חרמי כהנים does work.

keyTerms.meaning: Consecrating an item's value (for בדק הבית)
One may declare them חרם
Is it not that...? (opens a suggested reading)

phrases.english: We learned: 'One may consecrate them with a consecration of value,'
phrases.notes: 'Them' means animals already consecrated for the altar.

phrases.english: is it not that 'consecration of value' means for Temple upkeep,
and 'one may dedicate them' means for priestly dedications?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the ברייתא challenge is settled, the גמרא brings a new challenge from the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's ruling that attaching קדשי מזבח to חרמי כהנים does nothing.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה allows making altar animals חרם. If that means חרמי כהנים, then altar holiness can be attached to חרמי כהנים.

steps.title: Both words in the משנה mean Temple maintenance
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers in defense of רב הונא: both 'הקדש עילוי' and 'מחרימין' in the משנה refer to בדק הבית. The משנה is only teaching that either word works to dedicate to בדק הבית.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. Both of these are dedications for Temple maintenance. It makes no difference whether he uses the word 'consecrated' for Temple maintenance or the word 'dedicated' for Temple maintenance.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב הונא against the משנה from step 11. It says the word 'מחרימין' there does not mean חרמי כהנים at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קשיא assumed that 'מחרימין' means giving to the כהנים. The גמרא rereads it on רב הונא's behalf: 'מחרימין' here means using the word חרם to give the animal's value to בדק הבית. So the משנה is about two ways of speaking, not two places the value can go, and it never says קדשי מזבח can become חרמי כהנים.

keyTerms.meaning: This and that, meaning both cases
There is no difference
Using the word 'חרם' (dedicated) when making the dedication

phrases.aramaic: לָא, אִידִי וְאִידִי קׇדְשֵׁי בֶּדֶק הַבַּיִת,
phrases.english: No, both this and that are dedications for Temple maintenance,

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא שְׁנָא מַפֵּיק לְהוּ בִּלְשׁוֹן ״הַקֹּדֶשׁ״ לְבֶדֶק הַבַּיִת,
phrases.english: and there is no difference whether he says them with the word 'consecrated' for Temple maintenance,

phrases.aramaic: וְלָא שְׁנָא מַפֵּיק לְהוּ בִּלְשׁוֹן ״(חֶרְמֵי) [חֵרֶם]״ לְבֶדֶק הַבַּיִת.
phrases.english: or whether he says them with the word 'dedicated' for Temple maintenance.
phrases.notes: Some versions have חרמי, in round brackets; the corrected wording, in square brackets, is חרם.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא, אִידִי וְאִידִי קׇדְשֵׁי בֶּדֶק הַבַּיִת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא from the משנה in step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the source: 'מחרימין' is a way of speaking, not a separate category
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'מחרימין' means making the altar animal into חרמי כהנים.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both words dedicate to בדק הבית. The word חרם can also be used for בדק הבית.

steps.title: A ברייתא spells out that מחרימין means חרמי כהנים
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects רב הונא's reading. A ברייתא explains the same words openly: הקדש עילוי means בדק הבית, and מחרימין means חרמי כהנים.
steps.simpleTranslation: But that is not how it is taught. It is taught in a ברייתא: 'consecration of value' means dedications for Temple maintenance, and 'one may dedicate them' means dedications to the כהנים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב הונא's new reading from step 12. A ברייתא explains the משנה's words, and it says the opposite of what רב הונא said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא said both words mean בדק הבית. The ברייתא splits them: the first is בדק הבית and the second is חרמי כהנים. So the ברייתא shows that קדשי מזבח can become חרמי כהנים.

keyTerms.meaning: Dedicating the value of an animal (here, to בדק הבית)
Dedications that go to the כהנים

phrases.english: But that is not how it is taught,
as it is taught in a ברייתא:
'Consecration of value' means dedications for Temple maintenance,
'one may dedicate them' means dedications to the כהנים!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא לָא תָּנֵי הָכִי, דְּתַנְיָא בְּבָרַיְיתָא
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's reading that both words mean בדק הבית
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא explains the second word as חרמי כהנים, so the משנה really does allow קדשי מזבח to become חרמי כהנים.

steps.title: A second ברייתא: dedicating altar animals to the כהנים works
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא adds a second ברייתא, which says clearly that if someone dedicates קדשי מזבח to חרמי כהנים, what he did takes effect.
steps.simpleTranslation: Furthermore, it is taught: altar animals that he dedicated to the כהנים — what he did is done.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings an even stronger source against רב הונא. This ברייתא states the rule openly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 13's ברייתא was an explanation of words. This ברייתא gives the ruling directly: dedicating קדשי מזבח to חרמי כהנים works. That is exactly what רב הונא said does nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore; adds another proof
What he did is done; the act takes effect

phrases.english: And furthermore, isn't it taught:
altar animals that he dedicated to the כהנים —
what he did is done!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second, more direct source to the challenge in step 13.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's ruling that dedicating קדשי מזבח to חרמי כהנים does nothing
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא states openly that such a dedication takes effect.

steps.title: רב הונא is refuted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that רב הונא's view is refuted.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is a refutation of רב הונא; it is a refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא closes this back-and-forth and declares that רב הונא's position cannot stand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא has no answer to the two ברייתות. The final ruling is that קדשי מזבח can become חרמי כהנים.

keyTerms.meaning: A refutation; the view is shown to be wrong

steps.whatToRemember: Final ruling: קדשי מזבח CAN be dedicated as חרמי כהנים. רב הונא, who said it does nothing, is refuted.

phrases.english: The refutation of רב הונא is a refutation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sums up the challenges of steps 13 and 14.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב הונא is refuted; altar animals can be made into חרמי כהנים.

steps.title: But רב הונא had a verse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: רב הונא based his view on a פסוק, so how can he be refuted?
steps.simpleTranslation: But רב הונא said a verse!
steps.whatsHappening: The refutation leaves a problem: רב הונא's view came from a פסוק. The גמרא asks how we read that פסוק now, and this sets up עולא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A view based on a פסוק is not easily thrown out. If רב הונא is wrong, the גמרא needs another way to read the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: A verse from the תורה

phrases.english: But רב הונא says a verse!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the refutation of step 15 by pointing to רב הונא's verse.
steps.kashyaTarget: The conclusion that רב הונא is refuted
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רב הונא had a פסוק as his source, so the refutation seems to go against a verse.

steps.title: עולא: 'every חרם' includes everything
steps.stepSummary: עולא answers that the פסוק says 'כל חרם', every dedicated item. This teaches that a dedication to the כהנים takes effect on everything, even קדשי מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said: The verse says 'dedicated, every dedicated item'.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא gives a different reading of the פסוקים. The word 'כל' (every) shows that חרם takes effect on everything.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא read the פסוק as teaching that a חרם on קדשי מזבח stays 'לה׳' and never reaches the כהנים. עולא points to 'כל חרם' in the same פסוק (ויקרא 27:28), which includes every item. So the פסוק supports the ברייתות, not רב הונא.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Every dedicated item'; עולא reads it as including all items

phrases.english: עולא said:
The verse says: 'dedicated, every dedicated item.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 27:28. The word 'every' is what includes even altar animals.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר עוּלָּא: אָמַר קְרָא ״חֵרֶם כׇּל חֵרֶם״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 16 by reading the פסוק differently.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A different reading of the verse
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק leaves out קדשי מזבח, as רב הונא said.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'כל חרם' includes everything, even קדשי מזבח.

steps.title: Did עולא really say this? His ruling on attaching an עולה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions whether עולא holds this view. Elsewhere עולא said that one who attaches an עולה to בדק הבית creates only a 'holding back'.
steps.simpleTranslation: But did עולא say this? Didn't עולא say: one who attaches a burnt offering to Temple maintenance has only a holding back...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new challenge, this time against עולא. It quotes another statement of his that seems to clash with what he just said, and the quote continues past this section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since עולא lets קדשי מזבח become חרמי כהנים, he should surely let them be attached to בדק הבית too, because even רב הונא allowed that. But here עולא says attaching an עולה to בדק הבית gives it only an 'עיכוב', not a full dedication. That seems to contradict him.

keyTerms.meaning: One who attaches a dedication to an item
A burnt offering, which is a type of קדשי מזבח
Only a holding back; not a full dedication

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think this brings רב הונא back. The question now is only whether עולא contradicts himself.

phrases.english: But did עולא really say this?
But didn't עולא say:
one who attaches a burnt offering to Temple maintenance —
it has only a holding back

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אָמַר עוּלָּא הָכִי? וְהָא אָמַר עוּלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges עולא's reading from step 17 using another statement of his.
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's view that every kind of dedication takes effect on קדשי מזבח
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If עולא allows חרמי כהנים on קדשי מזבח, he should certainly allow בדק הבית. Yet he says attaching an עולה to בדק הבית gives it only an עיכוב.
